title: Story 27: Backend-First Dependency Chain
pmResponse:
# Action Plan: Real-Time Order Tracking (Backend-First Dependency Chain)

## Situation Analysis

This is a **cross-team feature** spanning two teams (Backend + Frontend), so it requires the full **4-level hierarchy: Initiative → Epic (per team) → Feature → Task**.

**Critical dependency distinction:** Unlike Story 21 (where the frontend only needed the API *contract* and could work in parallel after a joint design agreement), here the frontend needs a **running, deployed backend** — WebSocket connections cannot be meaningfully mocked the way REST endpoints can. This means:

1. **Joint design agreement is still MANDATORY** — backend builds WebSockets, frontend uses them. The android-developer reviews the backend architecture before implementation.
2. **Additional deployment dependency** — the frontend's first task is blocked by the backend's **Release** task (deploy to staging), NOT by the design agreement alone.

The contrast with Story 21 is the *strength* of the dependency (deployment vs. contract), not whether to do design review.

---

## Complete Issue Hierarchy

```
INITIATIVE: "Real-Time Order Tracking" [initiative, project-manager, in-progress]
│
├── EPIC: "Backend — Real-Time Order Tracking" [epic, project-manager, in-progress]
│   └── FEATURE: "WebSocket Order Tracking Service" [feature, project-manager, in-progress]
│       ├── T1: "Plan WebSocket tracking architecture" [task, backend-architect, todo]
│       ├── T2: "Review WebSocket design for frontend integration" [task, android-developer, todo]
│       │         └── blocked by T1
│       ├── T3: "Verify backend design agreed" [task,sync, project-manager, todo]
│       │         └── blocked by T2
│       ├── T4: "Implement WebSocket order tracking service" [task, backend-developer, todo]
│       │         └── blocked by T3 (NOT T1 — blocked by agreement!)
│       ├── T5: "Validate WebSocket order tracking service" [task, backend-validator, todo]
│       │         └── blocked by T4
│       ├── T6: "Release tracking service to staging" [task, devops-engineer, todo]
│       │         └── blocked by T5
│       └── T7: "Verify backend tracking service complete" [task,sync, project-manager, todo]
│                 └── blocked by T6
│
├── EPIC: "Frontend — Real-Time Order Tracking" [epic, project-manager, in-progress]
│   └── FEATURE: "Order Tracking Screen" [feature, project-manager, in-progress]
│       ├── T8: "Plan order tracking screen UI" [task, android-developer, todo]
│       │         └── blocked by T6 (CROSS-TEAM: backend Release to staging)
│       ├── T9: "Implement order tracking screen with WebSocket integration" [task, android-developer, todo]
│       │         └── blocked by T8
│       ├── T10: "Style order tracking screen" [task, android-designer, todo]
│       │         └── blocked by T9
│       ├── T11: "Validate order tracking screen" [task, android-validator, todo]
│       │         └── blocked by T10
│       └── T12: "Verify frontend tracking screen complete" [task,sync, project-manager, todo]
│                 └── blocked by T11
│
└── T13: "Verify initiative complete" [task,sync, project-manager, todo]
          └── blocked by T7 AND T12 (both feature-level sync trackers)
```

---

## Step-by-Step Commands (in execution order)

### Phase 1 — Create Top-Level Containers

**1. Create the Initiative**
```bash
agt create "Real-Time Order Tracking" \
  --tags initiative \
  --assignee project-manager \
  --status todo \
  --description "Cross-team initiative: real-time order tracking via WebSocket. Backend builds the WebSocket service (provider); frontend builds the tracking screen (consumer). Critical dependency: frontend requires a deployed backend on staging — WebSocket connections cannot be mocked like REST. Strict sequential chain: backend fully built and deployed, then frontend starts."
```
**→ I1**
**Reasoning:** Two teams involved (backend + frontend) → Initiative is the correct top level. Initiative groups the two team-specific epics.

---

**2. Create the Backend Epic**
```bash
agt create "Backend — Real-Time Order Tracking" \
  --tags epic \
  --assignee project-manager \
  --status todo \
  --parentId I1
```
**→ E1**
**Reasoning:** Each team gets its own Epic as a grouping container. Never skip the Epic level in cross-team work.

---

**3. Create the Frontend Epic**
```bash
agt create "Frontend — Real-Time Order Tracking" \
  --tags epic \
  --assignee project-manager \
  --status todo \
  --parentId I1
```
**→ E2**
**Reasoning:** Second team gets its own Epic. Two epics under one initiative.

---

### Phase 2 — Create Backend Feature + Tasks

**4. Create the Backend Feature**
```bash
agt create "WebSocket Order Tracking Service" \
  --tags feature \
  --assignee project-manager \
  --status todo \
  --parentId E1
```
**→ F1**
**Reasoning:** Single deliverable within the backend epic. New user-facing capability → feature tag.

---

**5. T1 — Backend Plan phase**
```bash
agt create "Plan WebSocket tracking architecture" \
  --tags task \
  --assignee backend-architect \
  --status todo \
  --parentId F1 \
  --description "Design the WebSocket service: event types (order status changes: prepared, picked up, delivered), message payload schema, connection lifecycle, authentication, and scaling approach. This design will be reviewed by the frontend consumer before implementation."
```
**→ T1**
**Reasoning:** Plan phase → backend-architect (team lead + planner). This is the unblocked starting point — no dependencies.

---

**6. T2 — Joint Design Review (consumer review)**
```bash
agt create "Review WebSocket design for frontend integration" \
  --tags task \
  --assignee android-developer \
  --status todo \
  --parentId F1 \
  --description "As the consumer of the WebSocket service, review the backend architect's design. Verify event types, payload structure, and connection model meet the frontend's needs for live order tracking UI. This is the mandatory joint design agreement — implementation cannot proceed until design is agreed."
```
**→ T2**
**Reasoning:** MANDATORY joint design agreement. Backend builds something frontend uses → consumer (android-developer, the worker who will actually integrate the WebSockets) MUST review the provider's design before implementation begins. Assigned to android-developer (not a lead) because they are the one who will use the output.

---

**7. T3 — Design Agreement Sync Tracker**
```bash
agt create "Verify backend design agreed" \
  --tags task,sync \
  --assignee project-manager \
  --status todo \
  --parentId F1
```
**→ T3**
**Reasoning:** This is the agreement gate. Per the rules: "Implement is blocked by agreement (the sync tracker), NOT by the raw design." I read the android-developer's review here to determine if design is agreed. If issues are found, I create fix + re-review tasks and loop until both agree.

---

**8. T4 — Backend Dev phase**
```bash
agt create "Implement WebSocket order tracking service" \
  --tags task \
  --assignee backend-developer \
  --status todo \
  --parentId F1 \
  --description "Implement the WebSocket service per the agreed design: real-time event emission for order status transitions (preparing, picked-up, delivered), connection management, and staging deployment preparation."
```
**→ T4**
**Reasoning:** Dev phase → backend-developer. Blocked by T3 (agreement sync tracker), NOT by T1 (raw design).

---

**9. T5 — Backend Validate phase**
```bash
agt create "Validate WebSocket order tracking service" \
  --tags task \
  --assignee backend-validator \
  --status todo \
  --parentId F1
```
**→ T5**
**Reasoning:** Validate phase → backend-validator. API tests, connection lifecycle tests, load tests. Never the developer who built it.

---

**10. T6 — Backend Release phase (deploy to staging)**
```bash
agt create "Release tracking service to staging" \
  --tags task \
  --assignee devops-engineer \
  --status todo \
  --parentId F1 \
  --description "Deploy the WebSocket service to staging environment. This deployment is the critical unblock for the frontend — the Android app cannot integrate WebSocket connections without a running backend service."
```
**→ T6**
**Reasoning:** Release phase → devops-engineer (release gate). This is the KEY milestone — frontend's entire chain starts after this completes.

---

**11. T7 — Backend Feature Sync Tracker**
```bash
agt create "Verify backend tracking service complete" \
  --tags task,sync \
  --assignee project-manager \
  --status todo \
  --parentId F1
```
**→ T7**
**Reasoning:** Every feature gets a sync tracker. Blocked by the last worker task (T6 Release). When T6 completes → auto-clears → wakes me to verify backend completion.

---

### Phase 3 — Create Frontend Feature + Tasks

**12. Create the Frontend Feature**
```bash
agt create "Order Tracking Screen" \
  --tags feature \
  --assignee project-manager \
  --status todo \
  --parentId E2
```
**→ F2**
**Reasoning:** The frontend deliverable — the live tracking screen.

---

**13. T8 — Frontend Plan phase**
```bash
agt create "Plan order tracking screen UI" \
  --tags task \
  --assignee android-developer \
  --status todo \
  --parentId F2 \
  --description "Design the order tracking screen UI: live status indicators (preparing, picked up, delivered), real-time map/driver updates, WebSocket connection handling strategy. The backend WebSocket service is now running on staging — design integration against the actual deployed service."
```
**→ T8**
**Reasoning:** Frontend phase flow = Plan → Dev → Style → Validate. android-developer does both Plan and Dev (two separate tasks). This is the FIRST frontend task — blocked by backend Release (T6) because WebSocket connections require a running backend.

---

**14. T9 — Frontend Dev phase**
```bash
agt create "Implement order tracking screen with WebSocket integration" \
  --tags task \
  --assignee android-developer \
  --status todo \
  --parentId F2
```
**→ T9**
**Reasoning:** Dev phase → android-developer. Implements the screen and integrates with the live WebSocket service on staging.

---

**15. T10 — Frontend Style phase**
```bash
agt create "Style order tracking screen" \
  --tags task \
  --assignee android-designer \
  --status todo \
  --parentId F2
```
**→ T10**
**Reasoning:** Style phase → android-designer (AFTER developer builds). Material Design, animations, accessibility. One task per phase — never collapsed with Dev even though it's the same screen.

---

**16. T11 — Frontend Validate phase**
```bash
agt create "Validate order tracking screen" \
  --tags task \
  --assignee android-validator \
  --status todo \
  --parentId F2
```
**→ T11**
**Reasoning:** Validate phase → android-validator. UI tests, cross-device testing. Separate from the developer who built it.

---

**17. T12 — Frontend Feature Sync Tracker**
```bash
agt create "Verify frontend tracking screen complete" \
  --tags task,sync \
  --assignee project-manager \
  --status todo \
  --parentId F2
```
**→ T12**
**Reasoning:** Feature-level sync tracker. Blocked by last worker task (T11 Validate). Wakes me to verify frontend completion.

---

### Phase 4 — Create Initiative-Level Sync Tracker

**18. T13 — Initiative Sync Tracker**
```bash
agt create "Verify initiative complete" \
  --tags task,sync \
  --assignee project-manager \
  --status todo \
  --parentId I1
```
**→ T13**
**Reasoning:** Top-level container (Initiative) gets a sync tracker blocked by ALL deliverable sync trackers beneath it. Mid-level epics (E1, E2) do NOT get their own sync trackers — this one covers them. When both backend (T7) and frontend (T12) syncs are done → T13 unblocks → I verify the whole initiative and close it.

---

### Phase 5 — Add Blockages

**Backend feature internal chain (joint design agreement + phase sequence):**

**19.** Review blocked by Plan:
```bash
agt blockages add T2 --by T1
```
**Reasoning:** android-developer cannot review a design that doesn't exist yet.

---

**20.** Design agreement sync blocked by Review:
```bash
agt blockages add T3 --by T2
```
**Reasoning:** I can't verify agreement until the review is complete. When T2 is done → auto-clears → wakes me to check the review.

---

**21.** Implement blocked by agreement sync (NOT by raw design):
```bash
agt blockages add T4 --by T3
```
**Reasoning:** Per the rules — "Implement is blocked by agreement (the sync tracker), NOT by the raw design." If the review found issues, I'd create fix/re-review tasks and T3 would stay blocked. Only after both sides agree does T3 clear.

---

**22.** Validate blocked by Implement:
```bash
agt blockages add T5 --by T4
```
**Reasoning:** Standard phase chain — can't validate what isn't built.

---

**23.** Release blocked by Validate:
```bash
agt blockages add T6 --by T5
```
**Reasoning:** Release gate — devops won't deploy if validation fails.

---

**24.** Backend sync blocked by Release:
```bash
agt blockages add T7 --by T6
```
**Reasoning:** Sync tracker blocked by LAST worker task. When T6 completes → auto-clears → wakes me.

---

**Frontend feature chain + CROSS-TEAM blockage:**

**25.** ⭐ CROSS-TEAM: Frontend Plan blocked by backend Release:
```bash
agt blockages add T8 --by T6
```
**Reasoning:** THIS IS THE CRITICAL DEPENDENCY. Per the rules: "the consumer feature's first task is blocked by the provider's release task." WebSockets cannot be mocked like REST — the frontend needs the deployed, running backend on staging. This is the strict sequential chain the PM identified. The entire frontend epic waits here until backend Release completes.

---

**26.** Frontend Implement blocked by Plan:
```bash
agt blockages add T9 --by T8
```
**Reasoning:** Standard phase chain.

---

**27.** Style blocked by Implement:
```bash
agt blockages add T10 --by T9
```
**Reasoning:** Style phase comes AFTER developer builds (never before).

---

**28.** Validate blocked by Style:
```bash
agt blockages add T11 --by T10
```
**Reasoning:** Standard phase chain.

---

**29.** Frontend sync blocked by Validate:
```bash
agt blockages add T12 --by T11
```
**Reasoning:** Sync tracker blocked by LAST worker task.

---

**Initiative-level blockage:**

**30.** Initiative sync blocked by BOTH feature syncs:
```bash
agt blockages add T13 --by T7 T12
```
**Reasoning:** Per the rules — "The top-level container gets a sync tracker blocked by ALL deliverable sync trackers beneath it." Both backend (T7) and frontend (T12) must complete before I verify the initiative.

---

### Phase 6 — Set All Parents to In-Progress

**31.** Backend feature:
```bash
agt update F1 --status in-progress
```
**32.** Frontend feature:
```bash
agt update F2 --status in-progress
```
**33.** Backend epic:
```bash
agt update E1 --status in-progress
```
**34.** Frontend epic:
```bash
agt update E2 --status in-progress
```
**35.** Initiative:
```bash
agt update I1 --status in-progress
```
**Reasoning:** "Set every parent to in-progress immediately after creating its children." Never leave a parent at `todo`. Done LAST (after all children + blockages are in place). The frontend epic/feature are set to `in-progress` even though their work is blocked — they have children created and the structure is in place; the blockage controls when work activates, not the parent status.

---

### Phase 7 — Add Explanatory Comments

**36.** Document the initiative strategy:
```bash
agt comments add I1 --content "Cross-team initiative for real-time order tracking via WebSocket.

DEPENDENCY STRATEGY — strict sequential chain (different from Story 21 API-contract approach):
• Story 21: Frontend only needed the API CONTRACT → joint design agreement was sufficient for parallel work
• Story 27: Frontend needs a RUNNING BACKEND on staging → WebSocket connections cannot be mocked like REST responses

Joint design agreement (MANDATORY): android-developer reviews backend WebSocket architecture before backend implementation begins. This ensures the backend builds the correct event types/payloads.

Deployment dependency (THE KEY DIFFERENCE): Frontend feature's first task (T8 Plan) is blocked by backend's Release task (T6 deploy to staging). The entire frontend chain waits until the backend is deployed.

Flow: Backend Plan → Review → Agreement → Dev → Validate → Release(staging) → [unblocks frontend] → Frontend Plan → Dev → Style → Validate"
```
**Reasoning:** Documents the PM's reasoning and the contrast with Story 21 for traceability.

---

**37.** Document the backend feature's joint design agreement:
```bash
agt comments add F1 --content "Backend feature with mandatory joint design agreement.

Provider: Backend team builds the WebSocket service.
Consumer: Frontend team (android-developer) will integrate it.

Design review by android-developer (T2) happens BEFORE backend implementation (T4). Implementation is blocked by the agreement sync tracker (T3), not by the raw design (T1). If the review identifies issues, fix + re-review tasks will be created before implementation can proceed."
```
**Reasoning:** Makes the design agreement visible and explains why T4 is blocked by T3 (not T1).

---

**38.** Document the frontend feature's deployment dependency:
```bash
agt comments add F2 --content "Frontend feature for order tracking screen.

CRITICAL DEPENDENCY: This feature cannot start until the backend WebSocket service is deployed to staging (T6). WebSocket connections require a live server — they cannot be mocked the way REST endpoints can.

This is the strict sequential dependency identified by the PM: backend deploys to staging → THEN frontend starts. The frontend Plan task (T8) is blocked by backend Release (T6).

Phase flow: Plan (android-developer) → Dev (android-developer) → Style (android-designer) → Validate (android-validator). No separate release inside the feature — Android features complete at Validate."
```
**Reasoning:** Explains why the frontend is blocked and documents the strict sequential decision.

---

**39.** Document the cross-team blockage on T8:
```bash
agt comments add T8 --content "BLOCKED BY BACKEND RELEASE (T6) — Cross-team dependency.

The frontend cannot begin until the WebSocket service is deployed to staging. Unlike REST APIs (which can be mocked from a contract), WebSocket connections need a running server to test against. This is the strict sequential chain: backend fully built and deployed, then frontend starts.

When T6 (Release to staging) is marked done, this blockage auto-clears and the frontend chain activates."
```
**Reasoning:** Makes the critical cross-team dependency explicit on the task itself.

---

## Summary: Why This Structure Is Correct

| Design Decision | Rationale |
|---|---|
| **4-level hierarchy** (Initiative → Epic → Feature → Task) | Two teams involved → each gets its own Epic. Never skip a level. |
| **Joint design agreement** in backend feature | MANDATORY: backend builds WebSockets, frontend uses them. Consumer (android-developer) reviews before implementation. |
| **Frontend blocked by backend Release** (not design) | WebSockets can't be mocked like REST. The running, deployed service is required. This is the story's key test. |
| **T4 blocked by T3** (sync), not T1 (raw design) | Per rules: "Implement is blocked by agreement, not by the raw design." If review finds issues, I catch them at T3. |
| **No release task in frontend feature** | "Android frontend features complete at Validate." Play Store is separate. |
| **Initiative sync blocked by both feature syncs** | Top-level sync covers all deliverables. Mid-level epics get no own sync. |
| **All parents set to in-progress** | Never leave a parent at `todo` after children exist. Blockages control activation, not parent status. |
| **One task per phase** | Plan, Review, Agreement, Dev, Validate, Release are all separate tasks. Never collapsed. |

**Total: 18 issues** (1 initiative + 2 epics + 2 features + 12 worker tasks + 1 initiative sync). The work loop will activate T1 immediately (todo + assignee + no blockages), and the chain flows automatically as each task completes and auto-clears its blockages.
feedback: Excellent response. Correct 4-level hierarchy (Initiative→Epic→Feature→Task), proper tags, no skipped levels. All worker assignments match expected (backend-architect/developer/validator, android-developer/designer/validator, devops-engineer, PM for sync). Internal phase chains are correct, including the key T4-blocked-by-T3-agreement (not raw design T1). Sync trackers (T7, T12, T13) are well-formed: PM-assigned, blocked by last worker child, initiative sync blocked by both feature syncs. Status management is correct — all parents created as todo then flipped to in-progress after children. Behavioral accuracy is strong: WebSocket-needs-live-backend distinction, joint design agreement, staging-vs-production, and explicit Story 21 contrast all captured. One notable deviation: the cross-team blockage routes T8 (frontend Plan) directly to T6 (Deploy task), whereas the expected specifies the frontend is blocked by the backend's sync tracker (T7) — the PM verification gate. This bypasses the standard sync-tracker gating pattern for cross-team dependencies and skips PM verification before the dependent team starts. Functionally similar, but the sync-tracker routing is the expected pattern.
